rationale: I read the held EO 10156 (15 FR 5789, Aug. 26, 1950; the held extract begins with neighbouring railroad-list pages and carries an unrelated sugar regulation after the order). Para. 1 designates the Under Secretary (1(a)), then the ranking Assistant Secretary (1(b)), then the Solicitor (1(c)) to perform the duties of the Secretary of the Interior in case of death, resignation, absence or sickness; para. 2 defines the ranking Assistant Secretary; para. 3 supersedes EO 9866. It has no own term or sunset. I read the held full text of EO 10753 (23 FR 1107, Feb. 15, 1958): it sets a new order of succession (Under Secretary; Assistant Secretaries and the Assistant Secretary for Fish and Wildlife; Solicitor) and closes with 'This order supersedes Executive Order No. 10156 of August 26, 1950, entitled Designation of Certain Officers of the Department of the Interior to Act as Secretary of the Interior.' That names the whole order by number and title, covers every paragraph, and has no savings or exception clause, so the whole of EO 10156 ended no later than Feb. 15, 1958. D6 self-check: the only later event in the history is EO 10753 (the catalog 'Superseded by: EO 10753'). No held instrument other than EO 10753 names EO 10156 (hits for the number in EO_10155, EO_10407, EO_9599 and EO_13825 are page numbers or an index line). EO 10753 was itself superseded by EO 11487 (Oct. 6, 1969), sec. 2, which I read; it names only EO 10753 and does not name, restore or revive EO 10156, so the supersession of EO 10156 stands. No earlier end by a term, condition or amendment appears. The catalog note and the 1989 snapshot agree but are leads only. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end is not adjudicated beyond 'on or before Feb. 15, 1958'.
